items.followUp: What is the least count of a digital Vernier Callipers, and name one dimension it can measure?

rubric.why: This identifies the instrument’s measuring purpose and its accuracy.
rubric.description: Defines Vernier Callipers as an instrument for accurately measuring small lengths.
rubric.how: Look for small lengths and accurate measurement.

rubric.why: Either value gives the least count of digital Vernier Callipers.
rubric.description: States the least count of digital Vernier Callipers.
rubric.how: Accept either equivalent value with its unit.

modelAnswer: Vernier Callipers are an instrument used to measure small lengths accurately, such as the internal or external diameter and depth of an object.
The least count of Digital Vernier Callipers is 0.01 mm (0.001 cm).

items.followUp: State the number of significant figures in 0.00450 and give one rule for identifying them.

rubric.why: These rules identify nonzero digits and captive zeros as significant.
rubric.description: States that all nonzero digits and zeros between nonzero digits are significant.

rubric.why: These rules distinguish leading zeros from trailing decimal zeros.
rubric.description: States that leading zeros are not significant, but zeros at the end of a decimal number are significant.
rubric.how: Look for the correct treatment of both kinds of zeros.

modelAnswer: Zeros between nonzero digits are significant.
Zeros to the left of the first nonzero digit are not significant.
Zeros at the end of a number to the right of the decimal point are significant.

items.followUp: Write the three equations of motion for a freely falling body, taking downward as positive.

rubric.why: This is the first equation of motion with acceleration due to gravity.
rubric.description: Writes the first equation of motion for motion under gravity.

rubric.why: These are the other two equations of motion with acceleration due to gravity.
rubric.description: Writes the displacement-time and velocity-displacement equations for motion under gravity.
rubric.how: Check for both equations using h (or equivalent displacement notation).

modelAnswer: Taking downward as positive, the acceleration is g.

items.followUp: Define limiting friction and write the relation between it, the normal reaction, and the coefficient of friction.

rubric.why: Limiting friction is the maximum friction immediately before sliding begins.
rubric.how: Look for maximum friction and the onset of sliding.

rubric.why: The coefficient of friction is the ratio of limiting friction to normal reaction.
rubric.description: Defines the coefficient of friction and gives its relation to the forces.
rubric.how: Check for the stated ratio or the equivalent verbal definition.

modelAnswer: Force of limiting friction (Fs) is the maximum frictional force that acts between two surfaces just before one surface starts sliding over the other.
The coefficient of friction (μ) is the ratio of limiting friction to the normal reaction: μ = Fs/Fn.
